_meta.description: Florida kitchen cost calculator inputs and multipliers. Planning only — not bids. Base dollar bands come from fl-cost-ranges.json (kitchen_remodel × size→scale).

disclaimer: Planning only — not a bid or contractor quote. These ranges are conceptual Florida planning bands for homeowner budgeting. They are not contractor-specific prices, guarantees, or formal estimates.
methodologyNote: Start from statewide Florida kitchen bands by approximate kitchen size, then apply relative multipliers for remodel depth, layout change, and finish level. Multipliers are relative planning factors, not market quotes. Location (ZIP/city) is for contractor matching only and does not invent local prices.
floridaNotes: Older Florida homes often need electrical capacity and ventilation upgrades when adding larger appliance packages.
Humidity, tile, and occupied-home phasing can add labor time versus a vacant gut.
HOA, coastal, and permit cycles vary by city and county — budget time, not just dollars.
Moving gas, plumbing, or load-bearing walls is usually the largest jump from a finish-only refresh.

sizeOptions.label: Compact / galley
sizeOptions.description: Smaller work zone or secondary kitchen

sizeOptions.label: Large / open-plan
sizeOptions.description: Island, open to living, or large footprint
sizeOptions.proxyHint: Often 250+ sq ft or a major opening into adjacent rooms

depthOptions.label: Cosmetic refresh
depthOptions.description: Paint, hardware, limited counters or fixtures — layout stays
depthOptions.explain: Refresh stays closer to a finish package when plumbing and cabinets are not fully replaced.

depthOptions.label: Mid-range remodel
depthOptions.description: Cabinets and finishes with limited layout change — most common path
depthOptions.explain: The baseline Florida kitchen remodel band assumes a real cabinet and finish package.

depthOptions.label: Full gut-rehab
depthOptions.description: Strip to studs; possible mechanical and layout moves
depthOptions.explain: Full guts raise demo, mechanical, permit, and finish coordination cost.

layoutOptions.label: Keep the layout
layoutOptions.description: Sink, range, and refrigerator stay put
layoutOptions.explain: Keeping wet and cooking locations limits plumbing, gas, and electrical relocation.

layoutOptions.label: Minor layout changes
layoutOptions.description: Small shifts without a new wet wall
layoutOptions.explain: Limited moves stay near the mid band when major plumbing runs stay.

layoutOptions.label: Major layout change
layoutOptions.description: Island, wall opening, or relocated wet wall
layoutOptions.explain: Islands and wet-wall moves add plumbing, electrical, and often structural work.

finishOptions.label: Basic / value
finishOptions.explain: Stock products pull the band down when the layout stays simple.

finishOptions.label: Standard
finishOptions.explain: Mid-market cabinets and surfaces are the baseline for these bands.

finishOptions.label: Premium
finishOptions.description: Higher millwork, stone, and appliance package
finishOptions.explain: Premium millwork and appliances move the high end faster than the low end.

education: Cabinet strategy (refacing vs full replace) is often the largest visible cost driver.
Plumbing or electrical relocation increases both dollars and schedule risk.
Occupied-home kitchens usually need more protection, phasing, and temporary cooking plans.
This tool does not invent contractor prices — get written bids from licensed Florida contractors.
